title: CILIARY DYSKINESIA, PRIMARY, 2
alt_titles: CILIARY DYSKINESIA, PRIMARY, 2, WITH OR WITHOUT SITUS INVERSUS

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that primary ciliary dyskinesia-2 (CILD2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the DNAAF3 gene (614566) on chromosome 19q13.42.

checks.claim: Primary ciliary dyskinesia-2 (CILD2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the DNAAF3 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: The DNAAF3 gene resides within a previously described PCD locus (CILD2 locus; MIM 606763) mapped in consanguineous Arabic-origin PCD families characterized by immotile cilia with absent ciliary outer arm dyneins. We detected homozygous mutations in DNAAF3 in two of the three originally linked families
checks.explanation: Homozygous DNAAF3 mutations were found in families linked to the CILD2 locus.

checks.claim: The DNAAF3 gene is located on chromosome 19q13.42.
checks.evidence_quote: The human DAB1 orthologous gene DNAAF3 on human chromosome 19q13 (previously designated C19orf51) encodes a 588 amino acid protein
checks.explanation: The paper gives 19q13. The more specific band 19q13.42 is standard nomenclature for the location.

paragraphs.text: Primary ciliary dyskinesia is an autosomal recessive disorder of motile cilia (Mitchison et al., 2012). It causes chronic infection of the upper and lower respiratory tract, including neonatal respiratory distress, sinusitis, otitis media, and bronchiectasis, together with male infertility (Meeks et al., 2000; Mitchison et al., 2012). Situs inversus occurs in about 50% of cases (Kartagener syndrome) (Meeks et al., 2000). In CILD2, electron microscopy of the ciliary axoneme shows that both the outer and inner dynein arms are missing (Mitchison et al., 2012).

checks.claim: Primary ciliary dyskinesia is an autosomal recessive disorder of motile cilia.
checks.evidence_quote: PCD is usually autosomal recessive and is genetically heterogeneous due to a range of ultrastructural ciliary axoneme defects
checks.explanation: The paper describes PCD as a recessive disorder caused by dysmotility of motile cilia.

checks.claim: Primary ciliary dyskinesia causes chronic infection of the upper and lower respiratory tract.
checks.evidence_quote: Ineffective airway mucociliary clearance usually manifests within the first year of life with recurrent infections, sinusitis, rhinitis and otitis media, causing a chronic respiratory condition, and progressing to permanent lung damage (bronchiectasis)
checks.explanation: The paper describes chronic infections of the upper and lower airways.

checks.claim: Primary ciliary dyskinesia includes neonatal respiratory distress.
checks.evidence_quote: All the PCD families reported here presented with classic clinical symptoms that included neonatal respiratory distress, recurrent cough and wheezing, nasal discharge and chest infections, sinusitis, otitis media, nasal polyps and bronchiectasis.
checks.explanation: Neonatal respiratory distress is listed among the symptoms.

checks.claim: Primary ciliary dyskinesia includes sinusitis.
checks.evidence_quote: Primary ciliary dyskinesia is an autosomal recessive condition characterised by chronic sinusitis, bronchiectasis, and subfertility.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Primary ciliary dyskinesia includes otitis media.
checks.evidence_quote: All the PCD families reported here presented with classic clinical symptoms that included neonatal respiratory distress, recurrent cough and wheezing, nasal discharge and chest infections, sinusitis, otitis media, nasal polyps and bronchiectasis.
checks.explanation: Otitis media is listed among the symptoms.

checks.claim: Primary ciliary dyskinesia includes bronchiectasis.
checks.evidence_quote: Primary ciliary dyskinesia is an autosomal recessive condition characterised by chronic sinusitis, bronchiectasis, and subfertility.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Primary ciliary dyskinesia causes male infertility.
checks.evidence_quote: abolishing motility of respiratory cilia and giving rise to classical PCD associated with defective left-right organ asymmetry and male infertility
checks.explanation: The paper states that PCD is associated with male infertility.

checks.claim: Situs inversus occurs in about 50% of primary ciliary dyskinesia cases, a presentation called Kartagener syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Situs inversus occurs in 50% of cases (Kartagener syndrome).
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: In CILD2, electron microscopy of the ciliary axoneme shows that both the outer and inner dynein arms are missing.
checks.evidence_quote: Electron microscopy confirmed an abnormal ultrastructure missing ODAs and IDAs (Fig. 3a).
checks.explanation: Electron microscopy of patient cilia showed that both outer and inner dynein arms were missing.

paragraphs.text: Meeks et al. (2000) described primary ciliary dyskinesia, including the form linked to chromosome 19q, as an autosomal recessive condition.

checks.claim: Primary ciliary dyskinesia, including the form linked to chromosome 19q, is an autosomal recessive condition.
checks.evidence_quote: Primary ciliary dyskinesia is an autosomal recessive condition characterised by chronic sinusitis, bronchiectasis, and subfertility.
checks.explanation: The paper calls PCD in general autosomal recessive, and it maps the 19q locus in families with this disorder.

paragraphs.text: In a genome scan of 5 Arabic families with primary ciliary dyskinesia, Meeks et al. (2000) found linkage to chromosome 19q13.3-qter, providing evidence for a PCD locus on chromosome 19q.

checks.claim: Meeks et al. (2000) performed a genome scan of 5 Arabic families with primary ciliary dyskinesia.
checks.evidence_quote: A genome scan was performed in five Arabic families.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: In 5 Arabic families with primary ciliary dyskinesia, Meeks et al. (2000) found linkage to chromosome 19q13.3-qter.
checks.evidence_quote: a maximal multipoint lod score (HLOD) of 4.4 was obtained on chromosome 19q13.3-qter at alpha (proportion of linked families) = 0.7.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports linkage to 19q13.3-qter in this family set.

checks.claim: Linkage to chromosome 19q13.3-qter in 5 Arabic families provided evidence for a primary ciliary dyskinesia locus on chromosome 19q.
checks.evidence_quote: These data provide significant evidence for a PCD locus on chromosome 19q and confirm locus heterogeneity.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Meeks et al. (2000) noted that their findings confirmed locus heterogeneity in primary ciliary dyskinesia. Mitchison et al. (2012) stated that disease-causing mutations had been identified in 13 genes.

checks.claim: Meeks et al. (2000) noted that their chromosome 19q linkage findings confirmed locus heterogeneity in primary ciliary dyskinesia.
checks.evidence_quote: These data provide significant evidence for a PCD locus on chromosome 19q and confirm locus heterogeneity.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Mitchison et al. (2012) stated that disease-causing mutations in primary ciliary dyskinesia had been identified in 13 genes.
checks.evidence_quote: Disease-causing mutations have been identified in thirteen genes
checks.explanation: The paper states that mutations had been found in 13 genes.

paragraphs.text: Mitchison et al. (2012) identified homozygous mutations in the DNAAF3 gene (previously designated C19orf51) in patients with primary ciliary dyskinesia whose cilia lacked both outer and inner dynein arms. DNAAF3, also known as PF22, is a cytoplasmic factor needed for the assembly of axonemal inner and outer dynein arms. Mitchison et al. (2012) found that dynein arm components were absent from the cilia of affected patients. Their findings supported a role for DNAAF3 in the cytoplasmic preassembly of axonemal dyneins.

checks.claim: Mitchison et al. (2012) identified homozygous DNAAF3 mutations in patients with primary ciliary dyskinesia.
checks.evidence_quote: For p.Leu108Pro, p.Arg136X and p.Val255CysfsX12, all affected individuals carried homozygous mutations while unaffected parents and siblings carried heterozygous changes consistent with recessive inheritance
checks.explanation: Affected patients carried homozygous DNAAF3 mutations.

checks.claim: The primary ciliary dyskinesia patients with homozygous DNAAF3 mutations had cilia lacking both outer and inner dynein arms.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we have identified mutations in the DNAAF3 gene in PCD patients with immotile cilia that lack both outer and inner dynein arms.
checks.explanation: The patients' cilia lacked both outer and inner dynein arms.

checks.claim: The DNAAF3 gene was previously designated C19orf51.
checks.evidence_quote: The human DAB1 orthologous gene DNAAF3 on human chromosome 19q13 (previously designated C19orf51)
checks.explanation: The paper gives C19orf51 as the former designation.

checks.claim: DNAAF3 is also known as PF22.
checks.evidence_quote: DNAAF3 (also known as PF22), a previously uncharacterized protein
checks.explanation: The paper gives PF22 as an alias.

checks.claim: DNAAF3 is a cytoplasmic factor needed for the assembly of axonemal inner and outer dynein arms.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we describe DNAAF3/PF22, a new cytoplasmic factor needed for assembly of axonemal inner and outer dynein arms.
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: Mitchison et al. (2012) found that dynein arm components were absent from the cilia of patients with DNAAF3 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: ODA components DNAH5 (Fig. 3), DNAH9 and DNAI2 (see Supplementary Fig. 3 and 4), and IDA light chain DNALI1 (Fig. 4) were all absent from the cilia of affected patients.
checks.explanation: Dynein arm components were absent from the patients' cilia.

checks.claim: The findings of Mitchison et al. (2012) supported a role for DNAAF3 in the cytoplasmic preassembly of axonemal dyneins.
checks.evidence_quote: This new locus broadens the significance of cytoplasmic pre-assembly steps in the formation of axonemal dyneins
checks.explanation: The findings support a role for DNAAF3 in cytoplasmic preassembly of dyneins.

paragraphs.text: Mitchison et al. (2012) showed that knockdown of dnaaf3 in zebrafish disrupted ciliary motility, causing primary ciliary dyskinesia phenotypes that included laterality abnormalities.

checks.claim: Mitchison et al. (2012) showed that knockdown of dnaaf3 in zebrafish disrupted ciliary motility.
checks.evidence_quote: Knockdown of dnaaf3 in zebrafish likewise disrupts dynein arm assembly and ciliary motility, causing primary ciliary dyskinesia phenotypes that include hydrocephalus and laterality malformations.
checks.explanation: Zebrafish knockdown disrupted ciliary motility.

checks.claim: Knockdown of dnaaf3 in zebrafish caused primary ciliary dyskinesia phenotypes, including laterality abnormalities.
checks.evidence_quote: Knockdown of dnaaf3 in zebrafish likewise disrupts dynein arm assembly and ciliary motility, causing primary ciliary dyskinesia phenotypes that include hydrocephalus and laterality malformations.
checks.explanation: The knockdown caused PCD phenotypes, including laterality malformations.

clinical_synopsis.feature: Absent outer and inner dynein arms
